cards.text: Ishmael, a man from the royal family, has struck down Gedaliah, the governor the king of Babylon appointed, and the people are afraid of the Chaldeans (Jeremiah 41:1-2, 18). So all the commanders of the forces, along with Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest, come to Jeremiah the prophet. They ask him to pray to the LORD for this remnant, because only a few of them are left out of many.

cards.question: The commanders and the people want Jeremiah to pray for them. What do they want the LORD to tell them?

answers.text: The way to walk and what to do
How long Babylon will rule them
Who their next governor will be

cards.question: Jeremiah promises the remnant he won't hold back a single word of the LORD's answer.

cards.text: Then the people tell Jeremiah, "May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act upon every word that the LORD your God sends you to tell us." Friend, that's not a pinky swear, that's signing your name in PERMANENT MARKER.

cards.question: The people promise to obey the LORD's voice whether His answer is pleasant or unpleasant. What do they say obeying will do for them?

answers.text: Make it go well with them

cards.text: After ten days, the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah. TEN DAYS, friend, and I can't wait ten minutes on a timer without cracking the oven door!

Jeremiah calls together Johanan, the commanders and all the people, from the least to the greatest, to hear the answer from the LORD, the God of Israel. Everybody packs in like the whole office when the boss says, "Quick announcement in the break room."

cards.question: The LORD's answer starts with an if. If the remnant will ___ in this land, He'll build them up and not tear them down.

cards.text: Build up, not tear down. Plant, not uproot. And God even says He'll relent of the disaster He has brought on them. Friend, back in that junk drawer I spent years in, I'd have said yes to an offer like that before anybody finished the sentence.

cards.question: The LORD tells the remnant not to be ___ of the king of Babylon.
The LORD tells the remnant they can stop fearing the king of Babylon because the king has gone back home.

cards.text: And it keeps getting BETTER. God says He'll show them compassion, and the king of Babylon, the very one they're so scared of, will show them compassion too.

cards.question: The LORD says He'll show the remnant compassion, and the king of Babylon will too. What does the LORD say comes with that compassion?

answers.text: Being restored to their own land
Being given a king of their own

cards.text: That's the good if. And you KNOW a second if is coming, because there's always a second if: what if the remnant says, 'We will not stay in this land,' and disobeys the voice of the LORD?

cards.question: The LORD's second if pictures the remnant saying they'll go live in the land of ___ instead.
In the LORD's second if, what does the remnant say they won't face once they're living in Egypt?

cards.text: No war, no ram's horn, no hunger for bread. Egypt sounds like a travel ad with a palm tree on it, but now comes the word of the LORD for the remnant of Judah, if they're determined to go there and live.

cards.question: The remnant fears the sword and dreads the famine. If they go to Egypt, what does the LORD say the sword and famine will do?
The LORD says not one of those who resolve to go live in Egypt will escape the disaster.

cards.text: Then God points back to Jerusalem: just as His anger and wrath were poured out on the people living there, He says His wrath will be poured out on the remnant if they go to Egypt. He says they'll become an object of cursing and horror, of vilification and disgrace.

cards.question: If the remnant goes to Egypt, what does the LORD say they will never see again?

cards.text: Jeremiah makes it plain: "The LORD has told you, O remnant of Judah, 'Do not go to Egypt.' Know for sure that I have warned you today!" Friend, that's a smoke alarm at three in the morning, as loud as a warning gets.

cards.question: Jeremiah looks back at how the people sent him to pray and promised to do whatever the LORD said. He tells them they have ___ themselves.
Jeremiah tells the remnant they have obeyed the voice of the LORD in everything He sent him to tell them.

cards.text: Jeremiah ends with a second "know for sure": by sword and famine and plague, they will die in the place where they want to go and live. We'll stop right here for now, friend, but this story's got more road ahead.
